title: A slower flow runs longer
hook: Halving a flow rate and doubling duration: what happens to volume?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Explain the offset between rate and duration under a fixed proportional change.

misconception: Half the flow rate always means half the volume.
objective: Explain the offset between rate and duration under a fixed proportional change.

claims.text: Hypothetical A is 12L/min for two minutes. B is 6L/min for twice A’s duration. Scaled model; illustrative:12L/min×t;6L/min×2t;constant flow.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At A-minutes=2min, A=24L and B=24L. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",12,"x"]; B=["*",6,2,"x"]; x denotes A-minutes. At x=2, A=24, B=24; recall at x=5: B=60. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions.

claims.text: The half-rate and double-duration factors cancel. Both deliver the same modeled volume. A rate reduction by itself does not state the final volume when the duration also changes.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",12,"x"]; B=["*",6,2,"x"]; x denotes A-minutes. At x=2, A=24, B=24; recall at x=5: B=60. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits.

claims.text: Hypothetical A is 12L/min for two minutes. B is 6L/min for twice A’s duration. Change only A-minutes to 5min. What is B (6L/min) now? Correct: 60L. Use B's stated rule with A-minutes=5min: it gives 60L. The half-rate and double-duration factors cancel. Both deliver the same modeled volume. A rate reduction by itself does not state the final volume when the duration also changes.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",12,"x"]; B=["*",6,2,"x"]; x denotes A-minutes. At x=2, A=24, B=24; recall at x=5: B=60. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

recall.question: Hypothetical A is 12L/min for two minutes. B is 6L/min for twice A’s duration. Change only A-minutes to 5min. What is B (6L/min) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with A-minutes=5min: it gives 60L. The half-rate and double-duration factors cancel. Both deliver the same modeled volume. A rate reduction by itself does not state the final volume when the duration also changes.
